verses.1: For the Chief Musician. Do not destroy. A maskil of David, when he sent word to Saul and the house of Saul sought to kill him.
verses.2: Deliver me from my enemies, God. Rescue me from those who rise up against me.
verses.3: Deliver me from evildoers, and save me from men of blood.
verses.4: For behold, they lie in wait for my life. They gather against me, strong men, though I have done no wrong, nor have I sinned, O LORD.
verses.5: Without guilt they run and set ambushes. Wake up to meet me, and see!
verses.6: And you, O LORD God of hosts, God of Israel, rouse yourself to punish all the nations. Do not show mercy to any evildoers. Selah.
verses.7: They return at evening. They growl like a dog, and circle the city.
verses.8: Behold, they speak with their mouths. A sword is in their lips. For who hears?
verses.9: And you, O LORD, laugh at them. You mock all the nations.
verses.10: My strength I will guard to you, for you are my God, my place of refuge.
verses.11: My God, his steadfast love will go before me. My God will show me in my enemies.
verses.12: Do not destroy them, lest they forget your law. Scatter them by your power, and bring them down, O my Defender, LORD.
verses.13: Their sin is in their mouths, the talk of their lips. Let them be caught in their pride. Let them be punished by their deception and falsehood.
verses.14: Consume them in wrath, destroy them, so that they may not exist. Let them know that God rules over Jacob, to the ends of the earth. Selah.
verses.15: They return at evening. They growl like a dog, and circle the city.
verses.16: They are scattered to eat. If they are satisfied, they will growl.
verses.17: But I will sing of your strength, and I will rejoice in your steadfast love at morning, for you have been my place of refuge, my shelter in the day of distress.
verses.18: My strength, to you I will sing. For you are my God, my place of refuge, my steadfast love.

notes:
Notes
- v. 1: The phrase "when he sent word to Saul and the house of Saul sought to kill him" is a historical title, explained in the context of 1 Samuel 19.
- v. 6: "Selah" is retained as is, since its function and meaning are unclear but it is a fixed feature in the text.
- v. 12: "Defender" is used for מָגִנֵּנוּ to convey protection, consistent with the root meaning.
- v. 14: "Consume them in wrath, destroy them" reflects the poetic parallelism of the Hebrew, with כַּלֵּה repeated.
- v. 17-18: The repetition of "my place of refuge" and "my steadfast love" reflects the psalmist's emphasis on divine loyalty and protection.

Notes
- v. 1: The phrase "when he sent word to Saul and the house of Saul sought to kill him" is a historical title, explained in the context of 1 Samuel 19.
- v. 6: "Selah" is retained as is, since its function and meaning are unclear but it is a fixed feature in the text.
- v. 12: "Defender" is used for מָגִנֵּנוּ to convey protection, consistent with the root meaning.
